title: Lightweight sampling and attribute tagger for inference SDK
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: Production inference traffic has a long tail of low-cost requests where full-span emission and heavy attribute enrichment increases p99 latency and storage cost. We need a standard, lightweight mechanism in our language SDKs and middleware that: 1) applies probabilistic and rate-limited sampling at the SDK edge, 2) attaches a compact set of high-value attributes (tags) to sampled and unsampled requests for downstream correlational metrics, and 3) exposes non-blocking enrichment hooks for the inference runtime (e.g., KV cache hit, batching decisions) without adding synchronous I/O or GC pressure.

Goals:
- Ship an SDK hook and middleware pattern that reduces tracing instrumentation overhead on hot request paths to <0.2ms median and <1.5ms p99 in typical Node/Go workloads.
- Provide a deterministic but tunable sampling policy (rate + reservoir + dynamic override by label) that is configurable per-tenant and per-route via Console.
- Standardize a compact tag schema (<= 12 keys, short names) for correlating traces with cost/latency dashboards (e.g., model_variant, batch_size_bucket, kv_cache_hit, route, sampling_reason).
- Ensure compatibility with our existing trace ingestion pipeline and minimal changes to downstream storage (use existing attribute prefixes).

Non‑goals: Full replacement of current server-side sampling or backfill of historical spans. This ticket focuses on SDK-edge behavior and the lightweight attribute tagging that enables better metrics without emitting full spans for every request.

Acceptance criteria:
- SDKs (Node and Go) have a pluggable middleware implementing sampling + tagger with clear tests and microbenchmarks.
- End-to-end benchmark showing overhead numbers and memory profile for a 1M requests/min workload with typical Redwood batching.
- Console config UI stub (read-only) for sampling rate and tag whitelist is wired to a feature flag.
- Documentation PR with example configs and migration notes for partners using custom instrumentation.
